Then discovered I needed my own key from an external AI provider. Options include most of the popular models including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google etc., or local models via LM Studio.</p><p id="8e79" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I used my existing paid Google Workspace account to access Gemini models. But here’s the thing — a non-technical writer wouldn’t have an API key lying around. They’d need to create an account with an AI provider, generate a key, copy it, paste it into Novelcrafter, and hope it works. That’s developer work, not writer work.</p><p id="73c9" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I finally figured it out after a couple of tries. Characters, locations, lore, items, magic systems, political factions, whatever your text heavy project needs.</p><p id="4ee1" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Unlike a basic story bible (Sudowrite) or Notes (Type.ai), the Codex is structured data that the AI actually reads. For series writers, this eliminates redundant data entry. Your world building carries forward from book one to book five without re-entering a single character description.</p><h3 id="5513" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Codex Catch-22 (The Honest Part)</h3><p id="f758" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Here’s what I struggled with. I added one Codex entry manually. And immediately felt frustrated. My manuscript already contains all the character details, plot points, and world building. Why am I re-entering information that’s already in my 40,000-word document?</p><p id="fe6b" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">This is the fundamental tension. If you add a few entries, the AI has half the context and the output suffers. But adding ALL entries means manually duplicating everything that’s already in your manuscript. That defeats the purpose.</p><p id="41ee" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Codex is brilliant for its intended use case: writers who build it <em class="qp">as</em> they write. You create a character, you add them to the Codex. You invent a location, you log it. Over time, the Codex grows alongside your manuscript. For series writers and world building obsessives, this is genuinely transformative.</p><p id="611a" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But for someone importing an existing manuscript? It creates a chicken-and-egg problem. Type.ai just reads the document. Novelcrafter wants you to re-describe what you’ve already written.</p><p id="d314" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I tried to be sneaky and ask it write the codex entries on my behalf — didn’t work. cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">AI Features: Bring Your Own Everything</h2><p id="ee00" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter’s AI features are fundamentally different from competitors. There’s no built-in AI. No proprietary model. You bring your own key, connect your own external AI provider, and choose your own AI models. This is either the best thing about the tool or the most annoying, depending on your tolerance for configuration.</p><h3 id="6e8c" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">What This Means in Practice</h3><p id="cb3b" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Want cheap testing? Use Gemini 2.5 Flash. Want premium prose? Use Claude Opus or GPT-5. Want free? Run local models via LM Studio on your own hardware. Want variety? OpenRouter gives you 300+ popular models.</p><p id="19a2" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">You’re not locked into anyone’s pricing or quality ceiling. You hold the dial.</p><h3 id="3f23" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">AI Chat</h3><p id="06a4" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Context-aware conversation with your manuscript. Add specific scenes, chapters, or Codex entries as context. Ask about plot holes, character consistency, pacing. The AI chat is genuinely useful once you understand context selection — which, as I covered, takes some figuring out.</p><h3 id="2f09" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Scene Beats and Prose Generation</h3><p id="aa88" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Write beats: short descriptions of what happens in a scene and the AI generates prose from them plus Codex context. Discovery writers can also use “continue writing” for more freeform AI generated content. It’s flexible, but the scene-based structure clearly favours plotters.</p><h3 id="1d1f" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">AI Scene Summarisation</h3><p id="434c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Auto-summarise scenes. Useful for keeping track of a <strong class="pn je">whole novel</strong> and maintaining consistency across chapters.</p><h3 id="d528" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Critical Insight</h3><p id="d231" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Here’s the thing I kept coming back to during testing: the underlying <strong class="pn je">AI models</strong> decide the quality, not Novelcrafter itself. I used Gemini 2.5 Flash. The output was good. The AI read my entire 40k+ word document and gave specific feedback referencing scenes, characters, and plot points from across the manuscript. Impressive.</p><p id="4f12" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But that credit goes to Gemini’s large context window, not to Novelcrafter’s architecture. If I’d plugged in a weaker model, the output would have been weaker. Novelcrafter gives you the kitchen. The meal depends on your chef and what you cook.</p><p id="7f9f" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Sudowrite pre-selects the chef (Muse). Type.ai hires a good one (GPT-5/Claude/gemini). Novelcrafter hands you the job listing and says “your call.” That’s a deep dive into flexibility but it also means the quality floor is lower if you choose poorly.</p><h2 id="4b45" class="qq qr jd z class="ph bv pi ot ou pj pk z b cr u w" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter alternatives</figcaption></figure><h3 id="e197" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter vs <a class="bx hw" href="https://ilampadman.com/recommends/typenovelcrafter" rel="noopener ugc nofollow" target="_blank">Type.ai</a></h3><p id="b212" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">This one is easier for me because I know where I stand. Type.ai is the friction-free option. Novelcrafter is not.</p><p id="74ce" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Type.ai is basically a writing tool with a lot of AI features sitting quietly and doing their job on the side until you need it. The editor stays at the centre. You load your manuscript, start working, and the AI can usually understand what’s already there without demanding that you first build a system around it.</p><p id="846c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Type.ai also has a context window of approximately 150000 words, good enough for an average Harry Potter sized book. So as you develop your story, it understands in depth what your story is. And mostly without you having to ask for it. But if you want AI help, it jumps and serves you the same as Novelcrafter (though not as flashy).</p><p id="58d3" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter is the opposite. It wants structure. Context. Codex entries. Model setup. It can absolutely become powerful once everything is wired up, but it does not meet you halfway in the same way.</p><p id="dfb5" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">That’s why Type.ai worked better for me personally.</p><p id="22de" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I already had a manuscript. I wanted the AI to read it, understand it, and help me think through it. Type.ai did that almost immediately. Novelcrafter made me work for it.</p><p id="5948" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Type.ai helps you keep writing. Novelcrafter asks you to build a system first.</p><h3 id="53d6" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter vs <a class="bx hw" href="https://ilampadman.com/recommends/sudowrite" rel="noopener ugc nofollow" target="_blank">Sudowrite</a></h3><p id="a9fc" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Sudowrite and Novelcrafter solve very different problems, even though they’re both aimed at fiction writers.</p><p id="677c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Sudowrite bundles everything. The AI is there, the Muse model is there, the credits are there, and the whole system is built to get you moving. It’s the easier tool to start with. You open it, learn how Sudowrite wants you to work, and the AI begins helping almost immediately.</p><p id="0e75" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter goes the other way. It gives you more control, more depth, and more flexibility but only after you’ve done the setup work. You bring the API keys, choose the model, wire up the context, and gradually earn your way into the value.</p><p id="2305" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">That’s the real difference.</p><p id="77c5" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Sudowrite is the guided option. Novelcrafter is the control-first option.</p><p id="ae6a" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Story Bible vs Codex comparison follows the same pattern. Sudowrite’s Story Bible is easier to understand and better at nudging you through story structure, character thinking, and early drafting. Novelcrafter’s Codex is deeper, more flexible, and much better for long projects, series, and heavy world building. But it also demands more from you.</p><p id="2113" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">So which one would I recommend?</p><p id="d3a2" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">If you want help getting moving, especially from a blank page — Sudowrite is the better pick.</p><p id="51db" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">If you want long-term control over a complex fiction project and don’t mind the setup pain, Novelcrafter is stronger.</p><p id="84a6" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Sudowrite has credit anxiety. Novelcrafter has setup anxiety. That really is the trade-off.</p><h3 id="a6ad" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter vs Google Docs</h3><p id="40b5" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Google Docs wins on one thing: everybody already knows how to use it.</p><p id="caf2" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">It’s free, familiar, collaborative, and frictionless in a way Novelcrafter simply isn’t. You open the doc and you write. That’s hard to compete with.</p><p id="342c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But for fiction? Google Docs is still just a document.</p><p id="46e7" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But honestly, Google may become more dangerous here over time. I wouldn’t be surprised if Gemini ends up more deeply embedded inside Google Docs in a way that starts to feel a lot closer to Type.ai. If that happens, the “write in Docs and let AI help in the background” workflow could become very compelling.</p><h2 id="3a29" class="qq qr jd z qs qt qu jz qv qw qx kc qy qz ra rb rc rd re rf rg rh ri rj rk rl cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Honest Pros and Cons</h2><h3 id="8b49" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Pros</h3><ul class=""><li id="0b1a" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Deep control once it’s working</strong><br>Novelcrafter gives you far more control than most AI writing tools. You choose the models, shape the workflow, and decide how much structure you want around the story.</li><li id="b38e" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">The Codex is genuinely powerful</strong><br>For world building, long projects, and series fiction, the Codex is the standout feature. It’s much closer to a structured story database than a simple notebook.</li><li id="b56c" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Excellent for complex fiction projects</strong><br>If you’re writing something big, messy, and continuity-heavy, Novelcrafter is built for that kind of work. Characters, lore, locations, evolving story states — it handles complexity well.</li><li id="e683" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Model flexibility is a real advantage</strong><br>You’re not locked into one AI model or one company’s pricing. If you want Gemini for cheaper testing, Claude for analysis, or something else entirely, you can do that.</li><li id="edc8" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Good value on paper</strong><br>The platform itself is relatively cheap, and if you’re disciplined with model choice, the overall cost can be lower than some all-in-one alternatives.</li><li id="b873" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Built for serious fiction writers, not generic content generation</strong><br>It clearly understands that novels, series, lore-heavy projects, and long-form consistency are different from pumping out random AI text.</li></ul><h3 id="8225" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Cons</h3><ul class=""><li id="98e3" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">The setup is harder than it should be</strong><br>This is the main problem. Before the tool becomes useful, you have to get through API keys, model selection, context setup, Codex confusion, and too many tutorials. That first hour is rough.</li><li id="eab3" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">It often feels like tool work before writing work</strong><br>Instead of helping you write immediately, Novelcrafter can make you feel like you’re configuring software. That’s a bad first impression for a writing tool.</li><li id="895a" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">The Codex can feel like homework if you already have a manuscript</strong><br>This is the catch. The Codex is brilliant if you build the project inside Novelcrafter from the start. If you’re importing an existing draft, re-entering story details can feel like duplicated effort.</li><li id="a00e" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">It expects too much prior knowledge</strong><br>The tool assumes you know what an API key is, what a Codex is, how context works, and why the AI can’t just see the whole manuscript automatically. A lot of writers won’t.</li><li id="dffb" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">The quality depends heavily on the AI model you choose</strong><br>That flexibility is a strength, but also a weakness. If the model is mediocre, the output will be mediocre. Novelcrafter gives you the system, not the guaranteed quality.</li><li id="a1d1" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Not friction-free at all</strong><br>If Type.ai is the friction-free option, Novelcrafter is the opposite. This is a tool for people who don’t mind earning the payoff.</li><li id="9ef0" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Too much tool for casual users</strong><br>If you write occasionally, prefer simplicity, or just want AI to help without setup, this is probably not the right fit.</li><li id="09ee" class="pl pm jd pn b jx ta pp pq ka tb ps pt pu tc pw px py td qa qb qc te qe qf qg sx sy sz cv" data-selectable-paragraph=""><strong class="pn je">Can feel unreliable in small but annoying ways</strong><br>Even once you understand the system, there’s still a sense that you have to keep an eye on what’s connected, what context is loaded, and whether the tool is really doing what you think it’s doing.</li></ul><h2 id="7d98" class="qq qr jd z qs qt qu jz qv qw qx kc qy qz ra rb rc rd re rf rg rh ri rj rk rl cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">My Verdict</h2><p id="8b0c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter is one of those tools that makes a bad first impression and a much better second one.</p><p id="2ba7" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The first hour is rough. The setup is clunky. The tutorials are too much. The AI doesn’t just “work” in the way a normal writer expects. You have to bring your own keys, understand the system, and figure out why the thing you assumed would happen isn’t happening.</p><p id="e9a0" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The whole point of a writing tool is to help you write, not make you feel like you’ve accidentally signed up for a lightweight engineering project.</p><p id="7002" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But — and this is the reason I didn’t write it off — once Novelcrafter starts working, the value becomes obvious.</p><p id="a36e" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The Codex is genuinely powerful. The model flexibility is real. The long-form memory can be impressive. And if you’re building a big, complex fiction project from the ground up, there’s a strong argument that Novelcrafter gives you more control than almost anything else in this category.</p><p id="f269" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">So my verdict is fairly simple:</p><p id="8634" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter is not the easiest tool to recommend. But it is an easy tool to respect.</p><p id="c6f4" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">If you want friction-free help, this is not it.<br>If you want the most guided option, this is not it either.<br>But if you want deep control over a serious fiction project and you’re willing to put up with the setup pain — Novelcrafter absolutely has a place.</p><p id="3a21" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">It just makes you earn it.</p></div></div></div><div class="am he ir qi qj qk" role="separator"><span class="ql ee bt qm qn qo"></span><span class="ql ee bt qm qn qo"></span><span class="ql ee bt qm qn"></span></div><div class="hr hx iz ja jb"><div class="am he"><div class="gg cs id ie if ig"><h2 id="1d2a" class="qq qr jd z qs qt tv jz qv qw tw kc qy qz tx rb rc rd ty rf rg rh tz rj rk rl cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Where I Landed Personally</h2><p id="d585" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I’m still sticking with Type.ai.</p><p id="c394" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">That isn’t because Novelcrafter is bad. It isn’t. In some ways, it’s probably the most powerful of the three tools I tested.</p><p id="359f" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">But I like friction-free work.</p><p id="96af" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I like opening a document, asking a question, and getting useful help without first thinking about API keys, model connections, context wiring, or whether I’ve built the right system around the manuscript. Type.ai fits that instinct much better.</p><p id="0a2c" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter asks for more from you. More setup. More structure. More patience. And for the right writer, that trade-off will be worth it. If you’re building a long series, maintaining a dense fictional world, or you genuinely enjoy having granular control over the whole environment, I can completely see why Novelcrafter would become your favourite.</p><p id="57cf" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I’m just not that writer.</p><p id="c2da" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">I tried the self-catering apartment. The kitchen was impressive. I can absolutely see the appeal. But I’m still the person who’d rather have room service.</p><p id="7278" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">That’s where I landed.</p><p id="1973" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx po pp pq ka pr ps pt pu pv pw px py pz qa qb qc qd qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">And honestly, that’s probably the cleanest way to think about Novelcrafter in general: not as the best tool for everyone, but as the right tool for a very specific kind of writer.</p><h2 id="97c7" class="qq qr jd z qs qt qu jz qv qw qx kc qy qz ra rb rc rd re rf rg rh ri rj rk rl cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Frequently Asked Questions</h2><h3 id="d785" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Is Novelcrafter free?</h3><p id="6aaf" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">No free plan, but there’s a 21-day free trial with all features unlocked. No credit card required. That’s more generous than most AI tools in this space.</p><h3 id="301e" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Do I need to be technical to use Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="6d8e" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">You need to set up an API key from an external AI provider. It’s not rocket science, but it’s not zero-friction either. If you’ve never configured an API before, budget about an hour for the initial setup including the learning curve of understanding what you’re connecting and why.</p><h3 id="5dba" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">What’s the best AI model to use with Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="8322" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Depends on your budget and priorities. Gemini 2.5 Flash for cheap testing. Claude Sonnet for quality prose. Claude Opus for premium output. All popular models are accessible via OpenRouter, which connects 300+ options.</p><h3 id="2376" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">How much does AI actually cost with Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="9620" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Users pay for AI tokens separately through their provider. Typical spend: $5–20/month depending on model choice and AI usage. Cheap models (Gemini Flash) can run under $5/month. Premium models (Claude Opus) will cost more per prompt.</p><h3 id="d57e" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Can I use Novelcrafter without AI?</h3><p id="a7b7" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Yes. The Scribe tier ($4/mo) has no AI — just writing and organisation tools. It works as a standalone novel writing platform. Think of it as a modern Scrivener alternative at that tier.</p><h3 id="2046" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Is Novelcrafter good for discovery writing?</h3><p id="a357" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">It supports it via “continue writing” beats, but the scene-based structure favours plotters. A discovery writer might find the rigid scene/chapter/act structure constraining. If discovery writing is your thing, you might prefer NovelAI or even just ChatGPT/Claude direct.</p><h3 id="023a" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Can I run local models with Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="c198" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Yes — connect via LM Studio or other models that can run on your machines. Free AI if you have the hardware. This is a genuine advantage for privacy-conscious writers or anyone who wants to avoid ongoing API costs entirely.</p><h3 id="35fa" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">How does Novelcrafter’s Codex compare to Sudowrite’s Story Bible?</h3><p id="e614" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Novelcrafter’s Codex is deeper — progressions, automatic context injection, wiki-like structure, series sharing. Sudowrite’s Story Bible is simpler and more guided. The Codex is more powerful; the Story Bible is easier to start. Different tools for different comfort levels.</p><h3 id="49dc" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Can I use Novelcrafter for non fiction?</h3><p id="b951" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">You <em class="qp">can</em>, but it’s overkill. The Codex and scene structure are specifically designed for fiction. For non fiction, Type.ai or a general AI writing tool is a better fit.</p><h3 id="90c4" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Does Novelcrafter have a mobile app?</h3><p id="7076" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Not yet. Browser-based only. It works on mobile browsers but isn’t optimised for it. If mobile writing is important to you, this is a real limitation.</p><h3 id="0cdc" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Can co authors work together in Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="d2e7" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Yes, on the Specialist tier ($20/mo). You can invite co authors, editors, and proofreaders into your project. Lower tiers are solo only.</p><h3 id="1252" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">What’s the biggest downside of Novelcrafter?</h3><p id="15c5" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">The initial setup. If you’re not comfortable with API keys and model selection, the first hour will be frustrating. Everything after that hour is significantly smoother but you have to survive the hour first.</p><h3 id="745f" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Is the generated content from Novelcrafter detectable as AI?</h3><p id="c25a" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Depends on the model, not Novelcrafter. Better AI models produce more natural generated content. Your line editing matters most — the more you revise AI output, the less detectable it becomes. This is true of every AI writing tool, not just Novelcrafter.</p><h3 id="02ef" class="rt qr jd z qs ru rv ao qv rw rx aq qy pu ry rz sa py sb sc sd qc se sf sg sh cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">Is Novelcrafter worth it in 2026?</h3><p id="32fa" class="pw-post-body-paragraph pl pm jd pn b jx ro pp pq ka rp ps pt pu rq pw px py rr qa qb qc rs qe qf qg hr cv" data-selectable-paragraph="">If you’re a serious fiction author who wants absolute control over your writing process and AI usage — yes. The Codex alone justifies the platform for series writers and world builders. If you want simplicity and zero friction — look at Type.ai. The right tool depends on the writer.</p></div></div></div></div></section></div></div></article></div><div class="am he"><div class="gg cs id ie if ig"><div class="ua ub am is do"><div
